children: Bank of England Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said on Tuesday that picture for domestic inflation pressure looked "relatively benign", adding that he was reassured by labour market and wage data.
"When I look at the domestic position, I think that's relatively benign
Particularly in the labour market I take quite a lot of assurance," Ramsden told lawmakers from parliament's Treasury Committee.

Megan Greene, an external member of the Monetary Policy Committee, told the committee she worried that an extended period of high oil prices could feed through into more persistent expectations for inflation in Britain's economy.
